exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean) after preterm induction with cervical ripening balloon (CRB)
outcome: insertion-to-expulsion time (IET) of cervical ripening balloon (CRB)
cohort: 82 women undergoing preterm induction with cervical ripening balloon between 2010 and 2021.
finding: Cesarean delivery patients had a significantly greater insertion-to-expulsion time (IET) of cervical ripening balloons and required more CRB removals at 12 hours, while the vaginal delivery cohort showed significantly greater dilation before and after CRB, with no differences in maternal comorbidities, induction indication, or neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery patients experienced significantly longer cervical ripening balloon (CRB) insertion-to-expulsion times compared to those achieving vaginal delivery, with spontaneous CRB expulsion and greater cervical dilation identified as potential predictors of vaginal delivery.
